instruction: Explain the concept of discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation.
response: "The DCF is a method for calculating the value of an investment, based on future expected returns and current prices.  It's not really about how much money you can make in the short term; it's more about what your net present value will be over time. The ""net"" part comes from the fact that you have to subtract out all the costs associated with the investment: taxes, fees, etc., which are usually ignored by most people when they calculate their own net worth. instruction: A company revenue increased by 20% from last year to $120 million. What was the revenue last year?
response: "The question is ""What was the revenue of your company in 2014?"". The answer depends on what you mean by ""revenue"" and how it's defined. For example: Net Income = Revenues - Expenses + Interest Charges - Taxes On Profit. So for this particular case, the revenues were $120M, so we can calculate our net income as follows: Net Income = $120M - ($35K * 6) - ($75K * 9) - ($80K * 12) - ($100K * 1) = $105K. This is not an exact calculation because there may have been other expenses that weren't accounted for here, but hopefully gives you some idea."

instruction: Explain the difference between revenue, profit, and cash flow.
response: "Revenue is what you get for selling something to someone else.  It's a measure of how much money you made from that sale. Profit is what you make after subtracting all your expenses (including interest on debt) from your revenue.   Cash Flow is just another way of looking at it - it's the amount of money in your bank account after all your expenses are taken out.  If you have $100 in your bank account, but only spent $50, then your cash flow would be negative (-$50).  This doesn't mean you lost money; it means you didn't spend enough to cover your expenses."

instruction: Explain why diversification can reduce investment risk.
response: "The idea of diversifying your portfolio is to spread out the risks in a way that reduces overall risk, not necessarily to reduce individual risks.  The reason for this is because you are trying to minimize the impact on your total return if any one stock or sector goes down.  If you have a large position in Apple and it drops by 20%, then you will lose money (and possibly more than that) but you won't be as badly hit as someone who has only a small position in Apple.  This is because there are many other sectors and companies that could drop by 20% without much effect on the market as a whole."

instruction: Explain the relationship between inflation and purchasing power.
response: "Inflation is a measure of how much money has been created over time, so it's not directly related to purchasing power.  It can be calculated by dividing GDP (gross domestic product) by the price level.  The price level is the average value of all goods and services in an economy at any given point in time.  So if you divide $100 billion by $250 billion, that gives you a percentage change in prices.  If you then multiply this number by the current price level, you get the annual rate of inflation.  This is what economists use as their primary metric for measuring inflation."

instruction: Why do banks need to maintain capital adequacy ratios?
response: "The primary reason for having a minimum amount of capital is that it allows the bank to withstand losses.  If you have $10,000 in your account and there's an unforeseen event (e.g., a fire or flood) that causes all of your deposits to disappear overnight, then you will be out of business.  You can't just ""pay off"" your customers because they don't exist anymore.  The only way to get back on your feet again is by getting more money from somewhere else.  This means that if you are not able to raise enough new funds through loans or other sources, then you may run into trouble.  In order to avoid this problem, you must have some sort of buffer against unexpected events.  Otherwise, you could end up being completely wiped out."

instruction: Explain how financial statements help investors evaluate a company.
response: "The balance sheet is the statement of assets and liabilities at a particular point in time, while the income statement shows what happened to those assets over that period (and also includes any cash flows from operations).  The net worth statement is an attempt to show ""what would happen if all your assets were liquidated today"" - it's not really useful for making decisions about whether or not to buy stock in a company.  It doesn't tell you anything about the future performance of the business."

instruction: Why can past stock performance not guarantee future returns?
response: "The reason that the market is so volatile is because it's a game of chance.  The more people who invest, the greater the risk of ""losing"" money.  This means that there are always going to be winners and losers in any given period.  It also means that if you have enough capital to invest, then you will make money over time.  If you don't, then you won't."

instruction: Explain the difference between active investing and passive investing.
response: "Active investors are those who try to pick winners by looking for ""gaps"" in the market, or trying to beat the market over a long period of time.  They do this by buying stocks that they think will perform well (or at least not lose money) based on their own analysis. Passive investors simply buy index funds like Vanguard's S&P 500 Index Fund (VTSAX), which is designed to track the performance of the entire US equity market. Active investors can be very successful if they have good intuition about what companies are going to do next, but it takes a lot more work than just buying an index fund."

instruction: A company has high profits but low cash reserves. Explain why this situation may happen.
response: "The reason for the ""low"" is that you have a lot of debt, and your assets are not enough to cover it all.  You need to pay off some or all of those debts before you can start making money again.  If you don't do so, then you will be in trouble."

instruction: Explain why Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies have highly volatile prices.
response: "Bitcoins are not a currency, they're just an asset that can be exchanged for goods and services in the same way as any other commodity.  They don't have to be used to buy anything; you could use them to pay your rent if you wanted.  The value of bitcoins is determined by supply and demand, much like gold or silver were during their heyday.  If there was more demand than supply, then people would want to purchase bitcoins at higher prices because it makes sense to do so.  This means that when there is less demand than supply, bitcoins will become cheaper since fewer people are willing to sell them for high prices.  When there is more demand than supply, bitcoins will become expensive since more people are willing to buy them from each other."
